title: Geometric Framework in R^d
content: The formalization defines points in R^d as EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), lines via base point + direction (parametric), and the rich/unblocked predicates generalized from R^2. These mirror the definitions in Erdos105Problem.lean but parameterized by dimension d.
mathContext: PointD d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d). LineD d has basePoint, direction (nonzero). contains: exists t, p = base + t * dir. isRich: exists p,q in A distinct on L. unblocked: no b in B on L.

title: Rich Line Existence (Proved)
content: rich_line_exists_d proves that any finset of >= 2 points in R^d has at least one rich line. The proof picks two distinct points p, q (using Finset.one_lt_card), constructs the line through them (base=p, dir=q-p), and verifies both points lie on it (t=0 gives p, t=1 gives q).
mathContext: For |A| >= 2, pick p != q in A. The line L = {p + t(q-p) : t in R} contains p (t=0) and q (t=1), so L is rich for A.

title: 2-Flat Structure and Rich 2-Flat Conjecture
content: A TwoFlat in R^d is parameterized by a base point and two linearly independent directions (dir1, dir2). A point p lies on it if p = base + s*dir1 + t*dir2. A 2-flat is rich if it contains 3 non-collinear points of A. The richTwoFlatConjecture asks whether obstacles can block all rich 2-flats.
mathContext: TwoFlat: {base + s*dir1 + t*dir2 : s,t in R} where a*dir1 + b*dir2 = 0 implies a=b=0. Rich: contains 3 non-collinear points of A (not all on a single line within the flat).

title: Obstacle Monotonicity (Proved)
content: Two monotonicity theorems: if a line (or 2-flat) avoids all obstacles in a larger set B, it also avoids all obstacles in any subset B' of B. The proofs are direct: unblocked means no b in B lies on the flat, so no b in B' (a subset of B) lies on it either.
mathContext: B' subseteq B and L unblocked by B implies L unblocked by B'. Proof: for b in B', b in B, so not on L.
